identity.title: The ALMA Spectroscopic Survey in the HUDF: The Cosmic Dust and Gas Mass Densities in Galaxies up to z ∼ 3

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using the deepest 1.2 mm continuum map to date in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field obtained as part of the ALMA Spectroscopic Survey (ASPECS) large program

targets.name: Hubble Ultra Deep Field (ASPECS LP 1.2 mm survey area)

evidence.quote: The ASPECS LP 1.2 mm survey covers 4.2 arcmin$^2$ in the HUDF, centered at $\alpha$ $=$ 3$^{\rm h}$ 32$^{\rm m}$ 38.5$^{\rm s}$ , $\delta$ $=$ -27$^\circ$ 47$\ensuremath{'}$ 00$\ensuremath{''}$ (J2000; 2016.1.00324.L).

redshift_or_distance.value: galaxy redshifts 0.3-5.5 (spectroscopic for 443 of 1481 catalogue sources, otherwise photometric)

evidence.quote: The ASPECS LP 1.2 mm survey covers 4.2 arcmin$^2$ in the HUDF, centered at $\alpha$ $=$ 3$^{\rm h}$ 32$^{\rm m}$ 38.5$^{\rm s}$ , $\delta$ $=$ -27$^\circ$ 47$\ensuremath{'}$ 00$\ensuremath{''}$ (J2000; 2016.1.00324.L).

distance_source.value: spectroscopic compilations (MUSE, HST grism etc.) and EAZY photometric redshifts from Skelton et al. 2014

evidence.quote: The ASPECS LP 1.2 mm survey covers 4.2 arcmin$^2$ in the HUDF, centered at $\alpha$ $=$ 3$^{\rm h}$ 32$^{\rm m}$ 38.5$^{\rm s}$ , $\delta$ $=$ -27$^\circ$ 47$\ensuremath{'}$ 00$\ensuremath{''}$ (J2000; 2016.1.00324.L).

question.value: How do the cosmic dust and gas (H2+HI) mass densities in galaxies, above given stellar masses, evolve with redshift up to z~3, from stacking the ASPECS 1.2 mm map at positions of H-band selected galaxies?

evidence.quote: we measure the cosmic density of dust and implied gas (H$_{2}+$H I) mass in galaxies as a function of look–back time.

bands.value: Band 6, 1.2 mm continuum from eight spectral tunings

evidence.quote: The ASPECS LP 1.2 mm continuum map was obtained by combining eight spectral tunings that cover most of the ALMA band 6.
The synthesized beam has a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of $1.53\ensuremath{''}\times1.08\ensuremath{''}$ at a position angle of $-84^\circ$.
The deepest region in the map (i.e., with a combined PB coverage $\gtrsim90\%$) has an rms of $9.5\,\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$.

other_facilities.name: HST (CANDELS, HUDF09/12), Spitzer IRAC/MIPS, ground-based optical/NIR

provided.value: Multi-wavelength master photometric catalogue (>30 bands) for stellar masses and H-band selection

evidence.quote: It provides measurements in $>\,$30 broad and medium bands for 1481 sources in the region of interest in the XDF

other_facilities.name: MUSE HUDF survey, HST grism and other spectroscopic surveys

evidence.quote: The spectroscopic redshifts of 443 of these galaxies were obtained from a variety of studies

what.value: Master photometric catalogue and photometric redshifts (EAZY)

evidence.quote: we use photometric redshifts determined in (cite: skelton_2014) by means of the `EAZY` code

what.value: Single-Schechter parameters of star-forming galaxy stellar mass functions

evidence.quote: The single Schechter parameters for the star-forming galaxy SMFs, as found in (cite: mortlock_2015).

what.value: Detected-source list for the ASPECS 1.2 mm map (22 sources) and astrometric offset

evidence.quote: There are 22 galaxies detected by Gonzalez–Lopez et al. (2019b) in the ASPECS LP 1.2 mm continuum map

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Semi-analytic and hydrodynamic dust/gas predictions (Popping 2017, Aoyama 2018, Li 2019, Vijayan 2019) compared with measurements

evidence.quote: we compare the cosmic dust and gas mass densities predicted by the semi-analytical model of (cite: popping_2017) for different stellar mass thresholds.

pipeline_or_manual.value: CASA calibration pipeline with the JAO script

evidence.quote: The data was calibrated with the Common Astronomy Software Applications (cite: mcMullin_2007) calibration pipeline using the script provided by the Joint ALMA Observatory (JAO).

task.value: CASA tclean, multi-frequency synthesis, mosaic of 85 pointings combined down to PB gain 0.1

evidence.quote: Imaging was also done in CASA using the multi-frequency synthesis algorithm implemented within the task TCLEAN, which combines all pointings together down to a primary beam (PB) gain of 0.1.
We used natural weighting and ‘cleaned’ down to 20 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ all sources with a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) greater than 5.
The synthesized beam has a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of $1.53\ensuremath{''}\times1.08\ensuremath{''}$ at a position angle of $-84^\circ$.
The deepest region in the map (i.e., with a combined PB coverage $\gtrsim90\%$) has an rms of $9.5\,\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$.

what.value: Survey strategy, calibration and imaging of the 1.2 mm map

evidence.quote: The survey strategy as well as the data calibration and imaging are described in detail by Gonzalez–Lopez et al. (2019b).

what.value: Master catalogue compilation and SED modelling

evidence.quote: The compilation of our master catalogue of galaxies and the modelling of their spectral energy distribution (SED) are described by (cite: decarli_2019) and (cite: boogaard_2019), respectively.

what.value: Gas-to-dust ratio and mass-metallicity relation parametrisation

evidence.quote: As in (cite: tacconi_2018), we used a gas-to-dust mass ratio ($\delta_{\rm GDR}$) that correlates nearly linearly with metallicity
As advocated by (cite: scoville_2016), we used a mass-weighted mean dust temperature of $\langle T\rangle_{\rm M}=T=25\,$K.
To this end, we used the empirical approach described in (cite: schreiber_2015).

analysis_steps.goal: Select H-band sample and stellar-mass completeness

method.value: Select H<=27 galaxies from master catalogue (555 galaxies); completeness limit from fitting L_H–M* power law plus 1 sigma scatter

evidence.quote: we kept only the 555 galaxies with an observed total[^3] $H$-band magnitude brighter than 27, of which 281 had a spectroscopic redshift.

key_parameters.value: Stellar masses from MAGPHYS using 0.37-8.0 um photometry plus 1.2 mm flux

evidence.quote: We used the galaxy’s photometry between 0.37$\,\mu$m and 8.0$\,\mu$m, as well as their 1.2 mm flux density (or upper limit).

fitting.value: M* = C L^alpha power law per redshift bin

evidence.quote: we fitted the correlation between the observed-frame $H$–band (1.6 $\mu$m) luminosities of galaxies and their stellar masses (derived as described above) with a simple power law

validation.value: Stellar mass functions agree with Mortlock+15 and Davidzon+17 above limits

evidence.quote: Down to our stellar mass–completeness limits, these stellar mass functions agree, within the uncertainties, with the fits inferred by (cite: mortlock_2015) and (cite: davidzon_2017)

analysis_steps.goal: Convert 1.2 mm flux to dust and gas mass

method.value: Optically thin dust mass equation (Kovacs 2010) with CMB correction; gas mass from metallicity-dependent gas-to-dust ratio

evidence.quote: In the optically thin approximation, which is almost always valid at the long wavelengths probed by our observations, the dust mass ($M_{\rm dust}$ in $M_{\odot}$) of a galaxy can be inferred
we used a mass-weighted mean dust temperature of $\langle T\rangle_{\rm M}=T=25\,$K

assumptions.value: GDR = 100 at solar metallicity, 12+log(O/H)=8.67; metallicity from mass-metallicity relation

evidence.quote: is equal to 100 at solar metallicity, $[12+{\rm log(O/H)}]_\odot=8.67$

validation.value: Varied T (15-35 K) and beta (1.5-2.0) to assess systematics

evidence.quote: a dust temperature range of $T\sim15-35\,$K implies a systematic uncertainty for our dust masses of 25%–50%.

method.value: 20"x20" stamps at galaxy positions (after astrometric offset), cut from clean mosaic for detected and residual mosaic for undetected sources, converted to density units per pixel, stacked per redshift bin and cumulative mass threshold

evidence.quote: The size of each stamp is 20$''$$\,\times\,$20$''$

key_parameters.value: Offset dRA=+0.076", dDec=-0.279"; PB coverage >75% (2.27 arcmin^2)

evidence.quote: we applied an astrometry offset ($\Delta$RA$=+0.076\ensuremath{''}$ , $\Delta$Dec$=-0.279\ensuremath{''}$)

key_parameters.value: Redshift bins 0.3-0.6, 0.6-1.0, 1.0-1.6, 1.6-2.3, 2.3-3.2; mass thresholds from 1e11 down in 0.5 dex steps

evidence.quote: starting at $10^{11}\,M_{\odot}$ and decreasing it in steps of 0.5 dex down to our stellar mass-completeness limit.

fitting.value: If S/N>=5 in 0.6xFWHM aperture, 2D Gaussian fit with free amplitude and widths; else total flux in 1.0xFWHM aperture; noise from 200 random apertures; Poisson term added in quadrature

evidence.quote: If $S_{\rm aper}/N_{\rm aper}\geq5$, we fitted the stacked stamp with a 2D Gaussian function.

validation.value: 200-realisation bootstrap, positional jitter of 0.6", randomised positions give non-detections

evidence.quote: As a last sanity check, we randomized the position of the galaxies in the sample and repeated the stacking analysis. We only obtained non-detections.

analysis_steps.goal: Model dust/gas-to-stellar mass ratio and extrapolate total densities

method.value: Fit rho(M*>M,z) = integral of f(M,z) x SMF with power-law f; per-bin and joint fits with redshift-dependent normalisation; extrapolate to M*>1e8

evidence.quote: Because the SMF of galaxies is well known up to $z\sim3$ (cite: mortlock_2015), one can solve for $f_{\rm dust}(M,z)$ by fitting $\rho_{\rm dust}(M_\ast>M,z)$.

key_parameters.value: f = A (M/10^10.7)^B; joint: log f = C + D log(1+z) + B log(M/10^10.7)

evidence.quote: {\rm log}(f_{\rm dust}(M,z)) = C + D \times {\rm log}(1+z)\ +

assumptions.value: Mortlock+15 star-forming SMF used; quiescent contribution negligible

evidence.quote: We did not use the SMF that includes quiescent galaxies, as the contribution of those to $\rho_{\rm dust}(M_\ast>M, z)$ has been shown to be negligible

fitting.value: Fit method/sampler not stated; reduced chi2 reported

evidence.quote: This fit described accurately our observations, with a reduced $\chi^2=1.0$.

validation.value: Compared to Tacconi+18 predictions, Dunne, Driver, CO surveys

evidence.quote: These predictions are in good agreement, within the total uncertainties, with our observations, but in our lowest redshift bin
Imaging was also done in CASA using the multi-frequency synthesis algorithm implemented within the task TCLEAN

used_for.value: SED modelling for stellar masses (high-z extension)

evidence.quote: using the high-redshift extension of the `MAGPHYS` code (cite: dacunha_2008; dacunha_2015)
we use photometric redshifts determined in (cite: skelton_2014) by means of the `EAZY` code
has an rms of $9.5\,\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$

Joint fit gas-to-stellar ratio parameters B, C, D

findings_qualitative.value: Low-mass galaxies (<~1e9.5-10 Msun) contribute little to cosmic dust and gas density; bulk is in star-forming galaxies with M*>~1e9.5

evidence.quote: The bulk of the dust and gas in galaxies appears to be locked in star-forming galaxies with $M_{\ast}\gtrsim10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$.

findings_qualitative.value: Popping+17 and Vijayan+19 models overestimate rho_dust at z<1

evidence.quote: they over-estimate the cosmic dust mass density in galaxies at $z<1$

claims.hypothesis: Do dust and gas densities converge to total values at the completeness limits?
claims.experiment: Cumulative stacking in mass thresholds per redshift bin
claims.finding: Completeness-limit measurements approximate total cosmic dust and gas densities in galaxies

evidence.quote: This flattening implies that at our stellar mass-completeness limits

claims.result: Decrease <5% to ~13% in rho_dust, <=10% in gas

evidence.quote: The contribution of quiescent galaxies – i.e., with little on-going star-formation– to the cosmic dust and gas mass densities is minor ($\lesssim10\%$).

claims.hypothesis: Does dust-based rho_gas agree with CO-based measurements and track the SFRD?
claims.experiment: Compare with ASPECS-CO and COLDz and scaled SFRD
claims.result: Good agreement in all redshift bins
claims.finding: Roughly constant star-formation efficiency within a factor ~2

evidence.quote: This confirms that galaxies have relatively constant star-formation efficiencies (within a factor $\sim2$) across cosmic time.

claims.experiment: Compare rho_dust evolution with dust yields from SFRD
claims.finding: ~90% of dust formed has been destroyed or ejected by z~0

evidence.quote: we infer that at $z\sim0$ about 90% of the dust that has been formed in the Universe must be destroyed

why_this_data.value: 1.2 mm probes Rayleigh-Jeans dust emission up to z~4; blind survey gives unbiased view of all galaxies

evidence.quote: The wavelength of this survey probes the Rayleigh-Jeans dust emission of galaxies up to $z\sim4$

why_this_method.value: Stacking at known positions of a mass-complete sample recovers emission below the detection threshold

evidence.quote: we can thus sum up their 1.2 mm emission within a given comoving volume, irrespective of their individual detectability in our 1.2 mm map.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: IRAC-selected samples rejected since they give shallower mass completeness than the H-band selection

evidence.quote: IRAC observations in the XDF do not provide stellar mass-complete samples as deep as that provided by the $H$-band.

limitations_admitted.value: Pencil-beam survey affected by cosmic variance (~42-58%)

evidence.quote: our estimates of $\rho_{\rm dust}$ are affected by cosmic variance, which is only partly included in the Poissonian uncertainties.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust-based gas may be biased against atomic phase; low-metallicity GDR relation uncertain

evidence.quote: This implies that dust-based gas mass estimates might be biased against the dust in the atomic phase.

referee_caveats_inferred: Gas masses depend strongly on assumed T=25 K, beta, kappa and metallicity-dependent GDR
Stellar masses and metallicities from mass-metallicity relation rather than measured
Cumulative bins are not independent and the extrapolation to 1e8 relies on a power-law f(M)
